original_date_notes: Exact first-publication date of the figure is not established by an inspected primary source. Context: the topic belongs to the Visual Basic 6.0 documentation set (asset namespace vbcon98). Microsoft announced Visual Basic 6.0 on 1998-06-15 with general availability scheduled for late summer 1998 (press release, evidence/pages/press_1998-06-15.html). Learn metadata ms.date 2007-01-04 is the MSDN migration date, not publication. The served GIF has Last-Modified 2021-04-23 (Learn archive upload). The 1998 printed Programmer's Guide on Internet Archive is controlled-lending (borrow) and was not accessed.
depicted_event_notes: Depicts the Visual Basic IDE in design mode (Project1/Form1) as documented for Visual Basic 6.0; capture date unknown.
access_method: Anonymous HTTPS GET of a public page and its image (no account, no terms click-through, no CAPTCHA). Raw response headers preserved in source/source-page/fig21_headers.txt; page HTML in source/source-page/aa733577.html.
identity_evidence: The image is Figure 2.1 of the Microsoft topic 'Starting the Visual Basic IDE', whose steps say to select Programs, Visual Studio, then 'Microsoft Visual Basic 6.0' and then state 'When you first start Visual Basic, you see the interface of the integrated development environment, as shown in Figure 2.1.' (source/source-page/aa733577.html, fetched 2026-09-15).

The page is filed under the Visual Basic 6.0 documentation archive: ms.prod visual-basic-6, mtps_version v=VS.60, depot MSDN.vb6-archive; the 2008 MSDN capture places it under MSDN Library > Visual Studio 6.0 > Visual Basic 6.0.

Visible content at full resolution: title bar 'Project1 - Microsoft Visual Basic [design]'; menus File Edit View Project Format Debug Run Tools Add-Ins Window Help; Toolbox (General tab), Form1 designer, Project Explorer 'Project1 (Project1)', Properties window with Alphabetic/Categorized tabs; Microsoft-drawn callouts Menu bar, Toolbar, Toolbox, Form designer, Project Explorer, Properties window.
It is not Visual Studio .NET: single-document VB IDE with classic intrinsic-control Toolbox, OLE container control, '[design]' caption, Win9x/NT4-style chrome.
identity_limits: No version number is visible inside the image itself. The VB6 identification rests on the image's publication in Microsoft's Visual Basic 6.0 documentation, not on appearance.

Documentation figures can be carried over from an earlier release; whether Microsoft captured these pixels from VB 6.0 or reused a Visual Basic 5.0 capture is not settled by the evidence inspected. The VB6-only Query/Diagram menus visible in the Wikipedia candidate are absent here, which is consistent with a standard project without Visual Database Tools active but does not prove the capture version.
